team.name: Air Defense Team
team.mission: Build autonomous robots that find and neutralize aerial threats and provide force protection through Lattice OS, an AI-powered 3D command-and-control center.

key_responsibilities: Shape Air Defense product and program strategy using rigorous data and user insights.
Conduct and lead UX research such as service blueprints, contextual inquiry, in-field rapid ethnography, focus groups, observations, workshops, surveys, and usability testing.
Use storytelling to inspire and align partners and key stakeholders.
Identify and drive forward ideas and recommendations to improve products based on actionable research insights.

Operationalize ways to consolidate and share research insights, communicate quickly and efficiently, synthesize insights into research repositories, and create workflows to work more powerfully with internal stakeholders.
Play an influential role in shaping the end-to-end experiences for critical operator workflows.
Help shape UX research best practices in Air Defense and share insights, process, and best practice across Anduril at large.

required: Bachelor's degree in Human-Computer Interaction, Human Factors, Psychology, Cognitive Science, Design, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of relevant user research experience working on digital products, able to work through ambiguity and help define research approaches that deliver impact based on actionable insights prioritizing the needs of the user and the business.
Research craft: can expertly design, plan, and execute research studies with clear objectives, goals, and timelines with little or no oversight.
Portfolio of work demonstrating research and insights that influenced both tactical and strategic product development work.

Strong communication skills in a fast-paced environment; ability to drive conversations with cross-functional partners with user data, helping bring user needs to the forefront while driving empathy through rigorous research findings.
Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret clearance.
preferred: M.S. or Ph.D. in Psychology, Human-Computer Interaction, Anthropology, Statistics, or other related area of study.
Active clearance: an active security clearance is helpful, but not required.
Group facilitation: can effectively lead co-creation, planning, and discovery workshops with cross-functional stakeholders.
Comfortable defining UX research capabilities in a fast-paced start-up environment, able to draw from a broad toolkit to integrate research into existing and future product roadmaps.
Programmatic support: opinionated about research operations and efforts to increase efficiency and improve decision making.
Is a good teammate: demonstrated proactiveness in helping to shape team culture and mentorship participation.
Hardware and/or Human Factors experience: development and research for hardware and service design, ergonomics, and/or support development of military standard systems.

Quantitative research skills: applying a variety of research methodologies to drive data-driven conversations and decision making, including scaled surveys, max-diff, and using programming languages to analyze data.

interview_process.status: Recruiter screen complete. Location preference, compensation expectations, and clearance eligibility are settled and closed.
remaining_stages: 30-minute conversation with the hiring manager, Dr. Daniella Kim, Head of Research.
Onsite loop of four back-to-back 1:1 interviews with engineering, design, and product partners.
Portfolio presentation, to be prepared separately at a later stage.

evaluation_levels.senior_uxr_baseline: Expertly designs and executes studies that produce actionable product and program insights.
evaluation_levels.lead_staff_uplevel_signal: Sets company-wide standards, bridges engineering latency with human perception, establishes frameworks before policy exists, defines Research Operations tools, and translates complex Human Systems Integration findings into hard hardware and software specifications.

evaluation_priorities: Meaningful Human Control in autonomous systems
Non-deterministic failure analysis and calibrated trust
Lead/Staff-level standard setting and cross-functional influence
